content.title: About
content.content: Breadfruit (Artocarpus altilis) is a large tropical fruit that resembles a bread‑like texture and flavor. When cooked—by boiling, baking, or frying—it becomes soft, aromatic, and mildly sweet. The fruit is a staple in Southeast Asian, Oceanic, and Caribbean cuisines.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: A single breadfruit can weigh up to 30 kg and measure over 30 cm in length.
Raw fruit is high in starch, which turns into easily digestible sugars when heated.
In traditional Oceanic cooking, breadfruit often replaces potatoes or rice.
A breadfruit tree can produce fruit for 20‑30 years with minimal decline.
Leaves and roots are used in folk medicine to treat wounds and colds.

items.title: Rich in complex carbohydrates
items.content: Cooked breadfruit provides slowly digestible starch that helps maintain satiety over time.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: One hundred grams of cooked breadfruit supplies about 15 mg of vitamin C, supporting immune function and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium aids fluid balance and normal heart function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Breadfruit contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and supports a balanced gut microbiome.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to breadfruit proteins.

items.title: High starch content
items.content: Large portions can cause a rapid rise in blood sugar levels for people with diabetes.

items.title: Toxicity of unripe fruit
items.content: Raw unripe breadfruit contains cyanogenic glycosides and must be fully cooked before consumption.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked breadfruit can be boiled in salted water, baked with herbs, pan‑fried, or added to soups and curries. It is often cubed and tossed into salads or served as a side dish.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked breadfruit in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Frozen portions retain quality for up to 2 months.
